primary.key: He who constantly thinketh upon Me, not thinking ever of another, of him I am easily reached, O Pârtha, of this ever-harmonised Yogî.
primary.s: After the yogi who departs uttering Aum, Krishna turns to the devotee of unbroken remembrance; Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 8.14, reads that ease as Krishna’s own work: unable to bear parting from such a devotee, he chooses him, ripens his meditation and clears its obstacles.
primary.src: Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 8.14, A. Govindacharya’s English translation (1898), archive.org gita-bhasya

basis.words: I, on My part, would not be able to bear separation of them … from Me; and therefore I Myself elect him (vrize). … carry to fruition the Meditation he adopts for reaching Me; … ward off for him the obstacles which may hamper him in his progress in Meditation
basis.gloss: I for my part could not bear to be separated from them, and so I myself choose him; I bring to fruition the meditation he takes up to reach me; I ward off for him the obstacles that could hinder his progress in meditation.

standby.key: Therefore verily there existeth, higher than that unmanifested, another unmanifested, eternal, which in the destroying of all beings, is not destroyed.
standby.s: Having told of beings pouring forth at Brahmā’s dawn and dissolving at nightfall, Krishna turns to what outlasts them; Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 8.20, reads the first unmanifested as ignorance, the seed of all beings, and the other as Brahman, the Imperishable, wholly different in nature.
standby.src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya, on 8.20, A. Mahadeva Sastri’s English translation, 2nd ed. (1901), archive.org bhagavadgitwith00agoog

basis.words: Being : the Supreme, the Para-Brahman, called the Akshara. … He is distinct from the Avyakta mentioned above, which is Avidya itself, the seed of the whole multitude of created beings ; that is to say, He is of quite a different nature from the Avyakta.
basis.gloss: The ‘other’ being is the Supreme, the Para-Brahman, called the Imperishable. … He is distinct from the unmanifested spoken of above, which is ignorance itself, the seed of the whole host of created beings; that is, he is of an altogether different nature from that unmanifested.
